The AI boom is not just a software story anymore. It is a $5 trillion infrastructure buildout — and it is hitting real-world limits.

Business Insider reports that hyperscalers will spend more than $5 trillion on AI technology and data centers through 2030. Right now, there are 1,500 active data center build sites across the United States. The ecosystem has grown large enough that specialized catering companies serve thousands of meals daily at individual construction sites.

But the constraints are real. Oracle issued a force majeure notice on its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico — a clear signal that even well-funded projects face delays. Community resistance to data center construction is getting louder and more organized. And on the global stage, BloombergNEF projects China will invest $3.9 trillion through 2049 to pipe renewable energy to coastal AI data centers.

For business leaders, this changes the planning equation. Your cloud provider's capacity, pricing, and availability are now functions of construction timelines, energy access, and local politics. If your AI strategy assumes unlimited cloud capacity at stable prices, those assumptions deserve scrutiny.
